subject: Security follow-up: pen test report request + vuln management cadence
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Security follow-up from our call — SOC2, pen test, vuln mgmt

Hi Sam — great to connect this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and the items you asked us to follow up on: 

1) SOC 2 status & GDPR/HIPAA posture
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation (report issued 2024-11-01). We can share the full report under NDA; summary available on request.
- We support HIPAA-covered workflows via our Private deployment and dedicated tenancy options; Data Processing Addendum (DPA) available for review.

2) Pen test report request
- You asked for evidence of third-party testing. We run an annual external penetration test and maintain an executive summary from the most recent engagement (2024). We can provide a redacted executive summary and/or schedule a controlled review under NDA.

3) Vulnerability management (SLAs / cadence / disclosure)
- Automated scanning: weekly internal automated scans (SCA + infrastructure) and monthly dependency scans.
- Internal pen testing: quarterly internal assessments; external third-party pen test annually and after major infra or scope changes.
- Remediation SLAs (typical): Critical: 24–72 hours; High: 7 days; Medium: 30 days; Low: next scheduled release.
- Responsible disclosure: we triage reports within 24 hours and aim to acknowledge reporters & provide status updates within 72 hours.

Next steps / asks from Acme: 
- Please confirm whether you prefer a redacted pen test executive summary or a restricted NDA review.
- Complete our vendor security questionnaire (link below) so we can populate any additional fields you need for procurement.
- I’ll loop in our security lead Rishi to coordinate the technical review.

Links/attachments: vendor questionnaire: https://docs.redwood.ai/vendor-questionnaire/ACME-2345
Attachments: Redwood_Security_OnePager.pdf (attached)

Would love to schedule a 30-min security review next week (Rishi + Neha from our side). Proposed windows: Tue/Wed 10:00–12:00 PT. What works for you?

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference
From: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security follow-up from our call — SOC2, pen test, vuln mgmt

Thanks Monica — that was helpful. A couple clarifying questions before we move to NDA: 

- For the pen test executive summary, can you provide a redacted PDF that removes tester identities and specific exploitation payloads but still shows scope, severities, and remediation status? That’s what our InfoSec review typically needs.
- On remediation SLAs: is the Critical 24–72h SLA contractual (SLA) or operational target? We need to understand which items are guaranteed vs. internal targets for our procurement and risk team.
- Do you have a history/log of open critical/high vulnerabilities over the past 12 months (counts & resolution windows)? A summary table is fine.

We’re also going to share a short procurement security questionnaire from our side — expectation is that you’ll fill in items around encryption-in-transit/at-rest, key management, and data retention.

I’m available Tue 10:30 PT for a review; if you can get us the redacted summary and an NDA link ahead of time, we’ll route internally.

—Sam
Sam Peterson
Head of Security Operations | Acme Health

To: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Security follow-up — looping security for answers + docs

On Fri, Jun 12, 2025 at 1:02 PM Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Monica — that was helpful. A couple clarifying questions before we move to NDA: 
> 
> - For the pen test executive summary, can you provide a redacted PDF that removes tester identities and specific exploitation payloads but still shows scope, severities, and remediation status? That’s what our InfoSec review typically needs.
> - On remediation SLAs: is the Critical 24–72h SLA contractual (SLA) or operational target? We need to understand which items are guaranteed vs. internal targets for our procurement and risk team.
> - Do you have a history/log of open critical/high vulnerabilities over the past 12 months (counts & resolution windows)? A summary table is fine.

Hi Sam — looping Rishi (Security Engineering) and Neha (Compliance) to respond to the technical/contract questions. Quick answers to start: 

- Pen test summary: yes, we can provide a redacted executive summary (scope, severity breakdown, remediation status). Full pen test reports are shared under NDA only. We’ll prepare a redacted PDF and mark any items that are still open.

- Remediation SLAs: the timeframes I listed are operational target SLAs we treat as commitments in our SOC/security runbooks. For procurement/contracting, we can discuss a contractualized SLA for specific critical items — that typically goes through dedicated contractual language in an MSA addendum. Let us know if Acme needs hard SLA language (we can engage legal).

- Vulnerability history: we can provide a summary table showing counts of critical/high/medium findings reported and average resolution windows for the last 12 months. We generally redact exploitable payloads and PoCs from the shared summary.

Rishi/Neha — can you confirm the suggested cadence and provide the redacted pen test exec summary (or confirm when it’ll be ready)? Also, please add a short note on our scanning stack (Snyk/Trivy/OS-level scans), and any customer-facing SLAs we should offer.

Thanks — Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-14T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security follow-up — pen test & vuln mgmt details

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. A few specifics from the security engineering side: 

- Pen testing cadence & scope: third-party external pen test annually (last completed Nov 2024). Scope typically includes public cloud infra, public endpoints, and core inference control plane. Internal red-team assessments take place quarterly.

- Redacted pen test executive summary: attached as Redwood_PenTest_Executive_Summary_2024_redacted.pdf. The doc includes scope, CVSS-based severities, mitigation status, and residual risk notes. Full reports are shared only under NDA.

- Scanning cadence and tooling: weekly automated vulnerability scanning (Trivy for container images, Snyk for dependencies), monthly software composition analysis, and continuous IaC scanning on PRs.

- Vulnerability management SLAs (customer guidance): Critical: acknowledge within 24 hours; patch/workaround pushed within 72 hours or emergency mitigation enabled. High: acknowledge within 48 hours; remediation targeted within 7 business days. Medium: remediation within 30 days. Low: next scheduled release cycle. If Acme requires contractual SLA windows we can discuss and map to support tiers.

- Historical summary: attached a one-page table showing counts/resolution windows for critical & high findings over the last 12 months (excerpted). We can expand this under NDA if you need more detail.

Attachments: Redwood_PenTest_Executive_Summary_2024_redacted.pdf; Vulnerability_History_12mo_excerpt.csv

If you want, we can run a short (30–45min) technical review next Tue 10:30 PT — I’ll bring logs/metrics and a sample remediation timeline for a recent critical fix.

-Rishi
Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@acmehealth.com>

- Please add a short paragraph to the pen-test summary that lists the remediation owners (team/function) for any open critical items — that helps our remediation acceptance review.
- Confirm whether the remediation windows you provided are something Redwood is willing to commit to in a security addendum (we’ll propose language in procurement).

Monica — can we lock in Tue 2025-06-24 10:30 PT for the technical review? If so, please send an invite and the NDA link so we can route internally before the call.

—Sam
